mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises risk-free rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months in at least 5 out of the last 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity and corporate capacity utilization, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO posts four consecutive >0.5% increases but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows at less than 50k per month signals labor market imbalances and overheating risks, which historically precede negative equity corrections over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes in at least 6 out of the last 10 instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% with a simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3% signals a rapid monetary policy normalization, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during at least 5 out of the last 8 such co-occurring spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months, irrespective of other conditions, is a reliable leading indicator of negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expected profit margin compression.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of such three-month RSAFS decline episodes, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (< -0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 100k per month and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market recovery, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m-o-m > 100000 AND UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 7 out of the last 10 such recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) contraction of more than 1% coupled with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 8% signals a synchronized downturn in manufacturing and construction, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to falling corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during at least 5 out of the last 7 such co-occurring industrial and housing downturns.
